But the finding over-claims twice in its own TEXT, not merely its lane note: 'including the ENTIRE character-animation layer' is FALSE (five of the nineteen web animdata blobs have no byte-identical android twin, and 14 of android's 18 MCSCharacter_* blobs match, not all 18), and the operative conclusion 'this makes EVERY <anim ... d="N"> duration an unqualified web-build CONTRACT' is therefore FALSE too. The skills-animation blob differs by 4,328 bytes and the spear blob by 20,988 - these are content differences, not padding. flinch d=8 survives only because it happens to live in 103, which is one of the matched files. The S0-3 caveat named as the target does fall, but only for the 21 enumerated files.

new_findings.text: A fourth hard, enumerable v0.682<->v0.717 divergence: the Writ of Release costs 25 gold in the shipped web client and 5 heavenly gold in the android data. The same 5x gap applies to the whole premium scroll tier - Amnesia Scroll (2200), Name Change Scroll (2207) and Clan Deed (2212) are all heavenlyprice 5 in android itemdata while the web shop grid badges its scrolls at 25. This CONFIRMS REBUILD_READINESS.md:216 rather than overturning it, and it is the concrete demonstration that C2's undischarged parity caveat has teeth on ECONOMY numbers, not just UI copy.

new_findings.text: The animation-data layer is NOT parity-clean. Fourteen of the nineteen web animdata blobs are byte-identical to an android twin; five are not - ogre, skills, guardian, spear and spider. The skills blob (which holds shunpo, flurry, deathtouch, spartakick, chargedshot) differs by 4.3 KB and the spear blob by 21 KB, so these are content differences, not padding. Any <anim d="N"> duration read from those five android blobs still needs a build hedge; only the fourteen matched blobs earn an unqualified web-build CONTRACT.
new_findings.lane_impact: L0 art-anim: the cheap machine-checkable parity instrument is real and worth keeping, but it must be run PER FILE. A blanket 'the animation layer is parity' licence would silently import android skill-animation timings into v0.717.

new_findings.text: The Focus meter's maximum is not the same in the two builds: 192 in web v0.717, 120 in android v0.682, and each build assigns it exactly once. That reframes the stance-switch numbers - the flat 48 the web build charges is maxreload/4, while android's graded cost is maxreload/6 (=20) with a maxreload/3 reset. So the two builds do not even share the same FRACTION of the bar, and any Focus config for v0.717 must use 192, not 120, and not a fraction ported from android.
new_findings.lane_impact: L-combat-core + L-skills-meters: skills-meters blocker (3) 'Focus numerics (max/fill/switch-cost)' closes on TWO of its three axes for v0.717 - max = 192 and switch-cost = 48 - leaving only the fill rate open. Nobody in this packet claimed the max.

new_findings.text: The web build's SoundManager declares the complete 43-name SFX inventory on a single line - no scraping of scattered call sites needed. Thirteen of those names have recovered waveforms via the android 122_Mobile_SoundResource decode (deflect, die1-3, slash1-3, punch, fart, hitmetal, goodkoto, refund, sumo), so the remaining 30 are the honest synth-target list.
new_findings.lane_impact: L7 audio: gives the art-anim-audio-feel lane a single authoritative cite for the event vocabulary and, joined to correction C3, an exact split between the 13 SFX with recovered audio and the 30 that must still be synthesized.
